name: Poland
summary: Two horizontal bands of white and red. The colours come from Poland's coat of arms, a white eagle on a red shield, and were declared the national colours in 1831.
origin: The white eagle on red has been the emblem of Polish rulers since the 13th century. Red and white were used as colours of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, though its flags varied.

On 7 February 1831, during the November Uprising against Russia, the Sejm declared white and red the national colours. The flag was officially adopted by the Second Polish Republic on 1 August 1919, after Poland regained independence.
The 1997 Constitution names white and red as the colours of the Republic. A law of 1980 sets out the flag's proportions and the version with the coat of arms.

facts: Monaco and Indonesia have the same colours with red on top; Poland's has white on top.
A variant with the coat of arms in the white band is used by embassies, airports and ships.
Polish Flag Day is 2 May, between Labour Day and Constitution Day.
clues: White over red, two horizontal bands.
Its colours come from a white eagle on a red shield.
Declared the national colours during an uprising in 1831.
Two other countries use the same colours upside down.
